text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - us-east-1b: elevated 5xx and ELB target health flapping. Paging SREs and infra. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/cases/1934567890

maria (SRE): seeing a clear spike in 5xx from north america users routed to us-east-1b. Dashboards show ELB unhealthy hosts in that AZ only.

ken (infra): can repro locally: `curl -v https://api.us-east-1.internal/health` -> intermittent connection reset, TLS handshake errors.

devon (eng-runtime): checking kube/host logs, seeing ENI RX/TX errors and a bunch of `net_err` in dmesg on i-0abc12345. Might be host NIC fabric.

sam (support): customer-reported slow/resets started ~10:28am ET, multiple support tickets spiked.

maria (SRE): Route53 healthcheck for api.redwood.ai (us-east-1b endpoints) is failing; global health still okay due to other AZs. Not failing over region yet.

ken (infra): running diagnostic: ```aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters 'Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1b' 'Name=status,Values=in-use' --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{Id:NetworkInterfaceId,Attach:Attachment.InstanceId,TxErrors:Statistics.TxErrors,RxErrors:Statistics.RxErrors}'``` CloudWatch shows elevated RxErrors for several ENIs.

devon (eng-runtime): ELB target-group `tg-frontend-us-east-1` -> us-east-1b targets show ~35% unhealthy, a/c are healthy. Connection resets and 502s.

maria (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily remove us-east-1b targets from TG to stop retries and customer impact 2) bias Route53 / ALB routing to us-east-1a/1c 3) open AWS support case and request AZ-level fabric check.

ken (infra): executing deregister now: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-frontend-us-east-1/abcdef123456 --targets Id=i-0abc12345 Id=i-0abc12346 Id=i-0abc12347```

incident-bot: action logged: ken (infra) removed 8 targets from tg-frontend-us-east-1 (us-east-1b).

devon (eng-runtime): shifting ALB weights to favor us-east-1a/c, monitoring latency and error rate. Streams show 5xx dropping but latency up ~20ms for a subset.

sam (support): status page: drafting update for customer-facing notice about partial degradation in us-east-1b.

maria (SRE): confirm: after removing targets 5xx rate down to near baseline but some latency increase. No wider region failover needed yet.

ken (infra): AWS Support case opened: 9876543210 - suspected underlying AZ networking degradation (ENI packet loss/host fabric). AWS acknowledged and is investigating host-level fabric in us-east-1b. No ETA yet.

devon (eng-runtime): kicking ASG surge to spin up replacement capacity in other AZs: ```aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name api-prod --desired-capacity 40 --honor-cooldown``` Should help absorb load while we keep 1b removed.

sam (support): will keep updating customers and tracking tickets. Suggest we mark affected customers in support with priority updates.

maria (SRE): draining plan in place — prefer draining out unhealthy hosts rather than immediate termination. Ken, started drains?

ken (infra): draining 6 hosts now via ALB connection-draining and cordon/drain if k8s-managed. Command: ```kubectl drain node/ip-10-0-1-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

incident-bot: severity auto-set to P1 based on impact and number of affected customers. Postmortem required.

ashley (oncall): I can take the next 30m handoff. Handoff summary: mitigations applied (targets removed, ASG surge on), AWS case open, monitoring for regression. Tagging postmortem owners.

maria (SRE): handing off to ashley. Notes for handoff: do NOT re-register original hosts until ENI metrics (PacketDropCount/RxErrors) are zero for 15 consecutive minutes and AWS confirms fabric stability.

ken (infra): quick update: CloudWatch shows two ENIs back to baseline, others still showing intermittent packet drops. Holding re-register.

devon (eng-runtime): suggestion for long-term: add per-AZ Route53 health checks + failover policy to move critical traffic to other regions automatically if an AZ-level fabric issue is detected for >10m. Add to postmortem.

maria (SRE): agreed. Adding to action items: per-AZ health checks, runbook update for deregister/re-register sequence, and improved ASG cross-AZ warm pool.

sam (support): published status page: "Partial degradation in us-east-1b affecting a subset of traffic; mitigation in progress. We are monitoring and will update as we have more info."

ashley (oncall): leaving instructions: monitoring window 30m, if AWS marks case as "root cause mitigated" we'll follow re-register plan: 1) confirm ENI metrics stable 15m 2) re-register 2 hosts at a time 3) monitor 10m windows for 5xx/latency and abort if spike.

maria (SRE): runbook snippet for re-register: ```for host in $(cat hosts_to_readd.txt); do aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=$host; sleep 120; ./check-health.sh $host || { aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=$host; break; }; done```

ken (infra): ack. tagging hosts with `incident/1934567890` and labeling for postmortem.

incident-bot: follow-up check scheduled in 15 minutes.

ashley (oncall): quick update 15m in - error rate holding at baseline, latency slightly elevated for a small subset. AWS case still open but support says they're seeing fabric perturbations and will push a fix on impacted hosts.

sam (support): continuing customer comms. Sent batch update to impacted customers.

maria (SRE): adding timeline notes to the incident ticket. We'll do a full blameless postmortem once AWS confirms final state.

ashley (oncall): leaving this thread open, monitoring. If anything changes I'll escalate. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
